a:r.a:t: RNA editing by alteration of nucleotides most commonly involves the enzymatic deamination of adenosine or cytidine residues.

p:cNvPr.descr: Structures of adenosine, inosine, cytidine, and uridine, and the deamination reactions which occur between them. (a) The diagram begins on the upper left with the structure of adenosine. It consists of a pentose ring (5-sided ring with an O on top as part of the ring). Its leftmost carbon bonded down to H and up to OCH2; the carbon below that bonds up to H and down to O. There are dashed lines representing a continuation of a molecule coming from these substituents. On the right, the carbon bonds up to a 5-sided ring, which is shares a double bond on the right with a 6-sideed ring. Together these make adenine. The apical N of the 5-sided structure double bonds down and left to C (not shown, but implied), which bonds down to N. N bonds right to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to the apical N. To the right is the 6-sided ring. Its apical C bonds up to NH2, and double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to N. N bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to the initial C. To the right of the adenosine is an equilibrium arrow. The top (pointing right) has a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of H2O and removal of NH3. The bottom (pointing left) arrow shows addition of NH3 and removal of H2O. To the right of the arrow is the structure of inosine. The pentose ring is the same as in adenosine; however, there is a key difference in the 6-sided ring above. Its apical N now double bonds up to O, and down and right to NH. NH bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to N. N bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to the initial C. All other aspects are the same as adenosine. (b) At the bottom left, the process begins with cytidine. The cytidine begins at the bottom with the pentose ring exactly as seen in adenosine. However, the carbon on the far right bonds up to a single 6-sided ring, cytosine. The carbon bonds up to the N at the very bottom of the ring. This N bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to C. C bonds up to NH2, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O. C bonds down and left to the initial N. To the right of the cytidine is an equilibrium arrow. The top (pointing right) has a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of H2O and removal of NH3. The bottom (pointing left) arrow shows addition of NH3 and removal of H2O. To the right of the arrow is the structure of uridine. Its pentose ring is identical to that of cytosine; the key difference is in the 6-sided ring. Its bottom N double bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to C. C double bonds up to O, and down and right to NH. NH bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O. C bonds down and left to the initial N.
